subject: Pricing & batching — follow-up and unit-econ
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Blum <sarah.blum@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & batching — follow-up and unit-econ

Hi Sarah — great chat today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have alignment before the SE call: 

1) Volumes & growth
- Current observed baseline you mentioned: ~2M tokens/month (pilot)
- Expected production target: 8–12M tokens/month within 3–6 months (you said ~10M as a target)

2) Unit-econ / budget target
- You mentioned a budget target in the ballpark of ~$30 / 1M tokens.
- Please confirm whether that target is gross spend or net of any reserved commitments.

3) Workload pattern + batching assumptions
- From the call: mostly short interactive requests (median request ~200 tokens, response ~150 tokens → ~350 tokens/request).
- Traffic is expected to be fairly continuous (steady daytime traffic across US), so continuous batching should be applicable.
- Key question: what is your acceptable 95th%-latency SLO for interactive flows? (we need this to size batching vs latency tradeoffs)

4) Next steps
- If you can share a 48–72hr anonymized traffic trace (arrival timestamps + request/response token sizes) that will let our SE run a benchmarking run and produce a tailored $/1M estimate under continuous batching assumptions.
- If you’re comfortable, we’ll produce a preliminary estimate for 10M tokens/month (range + assumptions) and send a short model walkthrough before the SE call.

High-level estimate (rough, subject to SE validation):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) with continuous batching & token-optimizations: ~$25–35 / 1M tokens at 10M tokens/month (depends on effective batching and average sequence length).
- Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit): ~$15–22 / 1M tokens (lower unit cost if you can commit and need predictable throughput).

I’ll attach a quick unit-econ workbook and a short pricing estimate. Can we schedule the SE deep-dive next week? I’m proposing Wed 9am PT but we’re flexible.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Camila — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: when I said ~$30 / 1M tokens I meant net operating budget (no reserved commit today). We can consider reserved if the performance/price tradeoff is compelling.
- Volume: we feel comfortable planning for 8–12M tokens/month; 10M is a good planning number.
- SLO: for our primary customer-facing flows we need 95th percentile <= 300ms for response start. We can accept up to 1s for background batch jobs.

I’ll ask our security team to send the SOC2 questionnaire — I’m attaching the initial questionnaire here so you can see the ask. Also, please include any SOC2 summary you can share on your end.

Wed 9am PT should work for a short 30–45m SE call — please send calendar invite.

Best,

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching — follow-up and unit-econ

Thanks Sarah — capturing the SLO and budget. Attaching the preliminary unit-econ workbook and a short pricing estimate (spreadsheet has line-item assumptions so you can tweak token lengths / arrival rates). Quick notes based on the 95th%-latency <= 300ms requirement: 

- Continuous batching works well when arrival rate is relatively steady (we can safely batch while keeping start-of-response latency under your 300ms target for most traffic shapes).
- Our conservative hosted estimate at 10M tokens / month under a 300ms 95th latency constraint is ~$28 / 1M tokens (includes heuristics for population-level batching and KV/prefix cache savings).
- If you move to a Dedicated pool with a monthly commit, we can get that closer to ~$18 / 1M tokens (numbers are illustrative — SE benchmarking will firm these up).

Assumptions included in the workbook (high level):
- Avg tokens/request: 350 (200 prompt + 150 response)
- Sustained average arrival rate: 4–6 reqs/sec across the fleet during peak windows (you can override this in the workbook)
- Effective batch size at that arrival rate: 8–14 requests depending on traffic burstiness → 20–35% token-cost reduction vs no-batching baseline
- Quantization & model selection: using an LLM variant compatible with INT8-style quantization for production inference (saves inference GPU runtime cost)

Next steps I’ll take today:
1) Send calendar invite for Wed 9am PT (30–45m) for SE benchmarking + pricing walkthrough.
2) Aditya — can you review the workbook and add any SE notes on expected batch sizes and hardware assumptions before the call?
3) Sarah — if you can share a 48hr anonymized trace (timestamps + token sizes) that will let us produce a firm benchmark.

Thanks — attaching: redwood_unit_econ_10M.xlsx, redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf.

—Camila

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching — follow-up and unit-econ (SE notes)

Adding a few SE-level notes based on the assumptions in the workbook and Sarah's SLO: 

1) Continuous batching tradeoffs
- With a 95th percentile start-of-response SLO <= 300ms, we can still batch aggressively for steady traffic. The key is to keep batch-accumulation windows short (e.g., 5–30ms) and rely on server-side preemption for tail requests.
- For FintechCo's expected profile (median request ~350 tokens, sustained peak ~4–6 reqs/sec), we expect effective batch sizes in the ~8–12 request range on modern A100/H100-ish serving backends. That maps to ~25–30% reduction in per-token GPU runtime compared to single-request execution.

2) Concurrency sizing
- If you use Hosted with autoscaling, target an instance pool sized to handle peak concurrent KV/cache state + expected burst concurrency. For the numbers above, plan for ~10–15 concurrent inference slots per shard to keep queuing low.
- Dedicated reserved capacity sizing will let us trade a monthly commit for lower per-token runtime pricing — we can model a 1/3 price improvement for a 6–12 month commit under typical utilization profiles.

3) Bench plan (recommended)
- Send a 48–72h anonymized traffic trace. We will run:
  a) Traffic replay at current concurrency profile
  b) Bench with continuous batching heuristics we intend to use in prod
  c) Produce a short report (expected latency distribution, median/95th, and $/1M tokens under hosted vs dedicated)

I’ll prepare the bench harness and test config once we have the trace. Happy to run an initial dry-run on synthetic traffic if you want a quicker preview.

—Aditya
